title: What is Tahajjud?
body:
Tahajjud (Arabic: تَهَجُّد) is a voluntary (Nafl) night prayer performed by Muslims after waking from sleep, between Isha and Fajr. It is mentioned in the Quran (17:79) and was a regular habit of the Prophet (ﷺ).

The Prophet (ﷺ) said that the best prayer after the obligatory prayers is the night prayer.

It is not obligatory, but it is a way to draw close to Allah in the quiet of the night, when few people are awake.

title: Best Times to Pray Tahajjud
body:
Tahajjud can be prayed anytime after Isha and before Fajr. However, the best time is the last third of the night. As reported in the hadith, Allah descends to the lowest heaven in the last third of the night and asks who is calling upon Him, so that He may answer.

To find it, count the hours from Maghrib to Fajr and divide them into three. The last part is the best time.

Many scholars say Tahajjud means praying after some sleep. If you cannot sleep first, you can still pray the night prayer.

title: Duas to recite in Tahajjud
body:
When the Prophet (ﷺ) got up at night to pray, he would begin by praising Allah. A well-known opening dua starts with Allahumma lakal-hamd (O Allah, all praise is Yours), and he would also ask for forgiveness and guidance.

  • Praise and glorify Allah (tasbih, tahmid, takbir) before you ask.
  • Make long sujood and ask for what you need there.
  • Ask for forgiveness. The Quran praises those who seek it in the hours before dawn (51:18).
  • Ask for the good of this life and the next: Rabbana atina fid-dunya hasanatan wa fil-akhirati hasanatan wa qina 'adhaban-nar (2:201).

title: How to wake up for Tahajjud regularly
body:
To wake up regularly, you need a combination of spiritual preparation, practical habits and a sincere intention.

  • Intend to pray before you sleep, and ask Allah to wake you.
  • Sleep early and avoid staying up late after Isha.
  • Do not overeat at night.
  • Make wudu and say your adhkar before bed.
  • Put your alarm across the room so you have to get up.
  • Start small. Two rakahs are enough, as long as you are consistent.

title: How many rakahs is Tahajjud?
body:
There is no fixed minimum or maximum. The Prophet (ﷺ) said the night prayer is prayed two rakahs at a time, and that the Witr is prayed to close it.

'A'ishah reported that he prayed eleven rakahs at night, including the Witr. Even two rakahs are a good start.

title: What is the Sunnah?
body:
The Sunnah is the way of the Prophet (ﷺ): what he said, did and approved. It explains how to put the Quran into practice, from prayer to character.

Some Sunnah acts are strongly recommended, and some are optional. All of them are a way to love him and follow him, and doing even a few consistently is a good start.

title: Sunnah prayers with the five daily prayers
body:
The Prophet (ﷺ) said that whoever prays twelve rakahs a day, other than the obligatory prayers, will have a house built for them in Paradise.

As listed in Tirmidhi, these are:

  • 2 before Fajr
  • 4 before Dhuhr and 2 after
  • 2 after Maghrib
  • 2 after Isha

The two before Fajr are especially emphasized.

title: Miswak and cleanliness
body:
The Prophet (ﷺ) said that if it were not hard on his Ummah, he would have commanded them to use the miswak before every prayer.

It is a simple Sunnah: use it when making wudu, before prayer, on waking up and before reciting the Quran. A toothbrush also fulfils the aim of keeping the mouth clean.

title: Sunnah of eating and drinking
body:
• Say Bismillah before you begin.
  • Eat and drink with your right hand.
  • Eat from what is in front of you.
  • Do not eat until you are overfull. The Prophet (ﷺ) taught that a few bites are enough to keep a person going.
  • Say Alhamdulillah when you finish.

title: Spreading salam and kindness
body:
The Prophet (ﷺ) told the believers to spread the greeting of salam among themselves. Saying As-salamu alaykum is a dua for peace, and replying is an obligation.

He also said that smiling at your brother is an act of charity. Small kindnesses are part of the Sunnah.

title: What are Hajj and Umrah?
body:
Hajj is the pilgrimage to Makkah and one of the five pillars of Islam. It is obligatory once in a lifetime for every Muslim who is able to make the journey (3:97), and it takes place on fixed days in Dhul Hijjah.

Umrah is a shorter, voluntary pilgrimage that can be done at any time of the year. It is not a replacement for Hajj.

title: The steps of Umrah
body:
• Ihram: put on the ihram and make the intention at the miqat.
  • Talbiyah: say Labbayk Allahumma labbayk. Labbayka la sharika laka labbayk. Innal-hamda wan-ni'mata laka wal-mulk, la sharika lak.
  • Tawaf: seven rounds around the Kaaba.
  • Sa'i: seven trips between Safa and Marwa.
  • Halq or taqsir: shave or trim the hair to finish.

title: The main steps of Hajj
body:
• 8th of Dhul Hijjah: go to Mina in ihram.
  • 9th: stand at Arafah, the heart of Hajj.
  • 9th night: stay at Muzdalifah.
  • 10th: stone Jamrat al-Aqabah, offer the sacrifice, shave or trim, and make Tawaf al-Ifadah and Sa'i.
  • 11th to 13th: stone the jamarat in Mina.
  • Farewell Tawaf before leaving Makkah.

The details differ by type of Hajj, so learn them with a trusted guide.

title: The Day of Arafah
body:
The Day of Arafah, the 9th of Dhul Hijjah, is the most important day of Hajj. The Prophet (ﷺ) said, 'Hajj is Arafah.'

Pilgrims stand in dua and dhikr from after noon until sunset. For those who are not on Hajj, fasting this day is highly recommended, and it is reported to expiate the sins of the previous year and the coming year.

title: Preparing for Hajj and Umrah
body:
• Make your intention sincere, for Allah alone.
  • Use halal money and settle your debts.
  • Seek forgiveness and make amends with people.
  • Learn the rites and the duas beforehand.
  • Prepare for the heat, the walking and the crowds.
  • Pack light: ihram, comfortable shoes and your essentials.

title: Why we fast in Ramadan
body:
Fasting in Ramadan is one of the five pillars of Islam. Allah prescribed it so that believers may attain taqwa, or God-consciousness (2:183), and Ramadan is the month in which the Quran was revealed (2:185).

The fast is from dawn (Fajr) to sunset (Maghrib), without food, drink or marital relations, together with guarding the tongue and the heart.

title: Suhoor and Iftar
body:
The Prophet (ﷺ) said there is blessing in suhoor, the pre-dawn meal. Even a few dates or a sip of water counts.

He would break his fast with fresh dates, or dry dates, or water. When breaking the fast, you can say Dhahaba az-zama'u wabtallatil-'uruq wa thabatal-ajru insha Allah. It means: the thirst is gone, the veins are moist, and the reward is confirmed, if Allah wills.

title: Laylat al-Qadr
body:
Laylat al-Qadr, the Night of Power, is better than a thousand months (97:3). It falls in the last ten nights of Ramadan, and the Prophet (ﷺ) told us to look for it in the odd nights.

Spend these nights in prayer, Quran and dua. 'A'ishah was taught to say: Allahumma innaka 'afuwwun tuhibbul-'afwa fa'fu 'anni (O Allah, You are the Pardoner and You love to pardon, so pardon me).

title: Voluntary fasts
body:
• Mondays and Thursdays.
  • The white days: the 13th, 14th and 15th of each lunar month.
  • Arafah: the 9th of Dhul Hijjah, for those not on Hajj.
  • Ashura: the 10th of Muharram, ideally with the 9th or 11th.
  • Six days of Shawwal after Ramadan.

title: Who may miss a fast?
body:
Allah does not intend hardship for the believers (2:185). A traveler or a sick person may miss fasts and make them up later (2:184).

Women on their period or in postnatal bleeding must not fast and make the days up later. Others, such as pregnant or nursing women and the elderly, have rulings that depend on the case, so ask a trusted scholar.

title: What is Hijamah?
body:
Hijamah, or cupping, is a traditional practice in which cups are placed on the skin to draw blood to the surface. It is done as dry cupping, with suction only, or wet cupping, where small cuts are made to let a little blood out.

It has been used for centuries, and it is mentioned in the Prophet's guidance on treatment.

title: Hijamah in the Sunnah
body:
The Prophet (ﷺ) is reported to have said that the best of the remedies you use is cupping. He is also reported to have had himself cupped.

Hijamah is a recommended treatment in the Sunnah, but it is not a replacement for seeing a doctor when you are ill.

title: Best days for Hijamah
body:
A narration reported in Tirmidhi mentions the 17th, 19th and 21st of the lunar month as good days for cupping. Scholars differ on how strong this report is.

Many practitioners prefer these days, and the morning on an empty stomach, as a matter of preference.

title: Before and after Hijamah
body:
• Choose a qualified practitioner who uses clean, single-use equipment.
  • Avoid a heavy meal before the session.
  • Drink water and rest afterwards.
  • Keep the area clean and covered as advised.
  • Avoid hard exercise for the rest of the day.

title: When to avoid Hijamah
body:
Talk to your doctor first if you take blood thinners, are anemic, are pregnant, have a bleeding disorder or a serious illness, or have low blood pressure.

Do not do hijamah on broken or infected skin. This article is general information, not medical advice.

title: What is Tawakkul?
body:
Tawakkul is relying on Allah fully, after doing your part. Allah says that whoever relies on Him, He is enough for them (65:3).

It brings calm: you take the means, and you accept the result as His decision, knowing it is good for you.

title: Tawakkul and effort
body:
A man asked the Prophet (ﷺ) whether he should tie his camel or leave it and trust in Allah. The Prophet (ﷺ) answered, 'Tie it, and trust in Allah.'

Tawakkul does not mean leaving effort. It means working hard, and then leaving the outcome to Allah.

title: Trusting like the birds
body:
The Prophet (ﷺ) said that if you relied on Allah as He should be relied upon, He would provide for you as He provides for the birds. They leave in the morning hungry and return full.

The birds still go out to look for their food. Provision comes to those who move, trusting in Allah.

title: What is Yaqeen?
body:
Yaqeen is firm certainty in faith, free from doubt. It grows with knowledge, reflection and experience of Allah's help.

Scholars often describe levels of certainty: knowing the truth, seeing its signs, and living it. The Quran speaks of these in terms such as 'ilm al-yaqin (102:5) and 'ayn al-yaqin (102:7).

title: Duas of Tawakkul
body:
• Hasbunallahu wa ni'mal-wakil: Allah is enough for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs (3:173). Ibrahim (peace be upon him) said it when he was thrown into the fire.
  • When leaving home: Bismillah, tawakkaltu 'alallah, wa la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah. It means: in the name of Allah, I trust in Allah, and there is no power or strength except with Allah.

title: Starting the day with adhkar
body:
Beginning the day with remembrance of Allah sets the tone for everything after it. The morning adhkar include Ayat al-Kursi (2:255), the last three surahs of the Quran, and istighfar.

You do not need to do everything. A few minutes after Fajr, done every day, is better than a long session that you drop.

title: Guarding the five prayers
body:
Prayer is the pillar of the religion, so plan your day around it, not the other way round. Allah calls the believers to guard their prayers (2:238).

  • Pray at the start of the time when you can.
  • Set the prayer times on your phone.
  • Pray in congregation whenever possible.

title: The Sunnah way of sleeping
body:
• Make wudu before you sleep.
  • Lie on your right side.
  • Recite Ayat al-Kursi, as reported to bring protection through the night.
  • Say Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya (in Your name, O Allah, I die and I live).

title: Small deeds that last
body:
The Prophet (ﷺ) said the most beloved deeds to Allah are those done consistently, even if they are small.

Pick one or two small habits, such as a page of Quran or morning adhkar, and keep them going. Add more only once they feel natural.

title: Gratitude and patience
body:
The Prophet (ﷺ) said that the affair of the believer is amazing: if good comes, they are grateful, and that is good for them. If hardship comes, they are patient, and that is good for them.

Gratitude (shukr) and patience (sabr) turn every situation into a chance for reward. A simple habit is to end each day by naming a few blessings.
